name: How do sliding windows compare to casement windows in terms of energy efficiency?

mainEntity.name: How do sliding windows compare to casement windows in terms of energy efficiency?

acceptedAnswer.text: Sliding windows typically have a slightly lower energy efficiency rating than casement windows due to their design, which relies on a meeting rail and weatherstripping rather than a compression seal. Casement windows seal tightly on all four sides when cranked shut, creating a more airtight barrier. However, modern sliding windows, especially those with advanced glazing and tight seals, can still offer good energy performance. The practical tradeoff is often between the ease of operation and view provided by sliders versus the superior sealing of casements.
acceptedAnswer.description: Casement windows generally offer better energy efficiency due to a tighter compression seal, while modern sliding windows still provide good performance with different operational benefits.
